name: Wai'ao Beach
hazards: boulders near shore;rocks hidden at high tide;closeouts;no swimming near the harbour
facilities: surf shops;board rental;surf schools;paid showers;parking;train station;cafes
description: Wai'ao is a long black-sand beach break on the northeast coast of Yilan County, just north of Toucheng and about an hour by car or train from Taipei. Waves break both left and right as A-frame peaks, and the best surfing is usually at the southern end near the outer wall of Wushi Harbor. It suits beginners on small swells and better surfers when the swell is bigger; summer brings small, easy waves, while autumn and winter north-east monsoon swells are larger. Typical swell is around 2 to 6 feet, and mid to high tide works best. Watch for large boulders near the shore, smaller rocks hidden at high tide, and closeouts when the sandbar is poor. It is one of the busiest surf beaches in Taiwan, especially on summer weekends, with many surf shops, schools and board rentals, paid showers in the visitor center basement, parking and Wai'ao train station nearby.

name: Jinzun Harbor
description: Jinzun is a point break at Jinzun Harbor in Donghe Township, Taitung County, about 10 minutes north of Dulan on the east coast. The wave formed after the harbour breakwalls were built more than 40 years ago and breaks as consistent A-frame peaks, with a left and a right, over a cobblestone bottom. It is considered one of the best surf spots in Taiwan and hosts the World Surf League Taiwan Open of Surfing every November. The waves are playful but powerful enough for performance surfing and are rated for intermediate and better surfers. It works best on swell from the east, northeast, southeast or south, with westerly offshore wind and mid tide; autumn and winter north-east monsoon swells bring the biggest waves.

name: Jialeshuei
description: Jialeshuei is a beach break with A-frame waves on the east side of the Hengchun Peninsula in Manzhou Township, on the opposite side of the peninsula from the busy Kenting beaches. It is known for consistent waves all year and is often recommended for beginners, while stronger winds and bigger surf from November to March suit experienced surfers. Early morning usually has less choppy waves. It is quieter than the Kenting side and has many surf schools offering lessons and board rental, plus guesthouses and hostels nearby. The Manzhou Jialeshui International Surfing Festival is held here every October.

name: Cijin Beach
description: Cijin Beach is a roughly 1.5 km stretch of black sand on the northwestern side of Cijin Island, facing the Taiwan Strait. It is a beach break with A-frame peaks that is commonly rated as suitable for beginners. Surf shops with board rental cluster at the western end of the beach on Miaoqian Road Lane 1, and surf schools offer lessons that include instructor, board rental and showers. Free showers and a beach bar are available. Swimming and surfing are allowed most of the time, but swimming may be closed in winter or when the current is strong. The beach is reached by the ferry from Gushan Ferry Pier in Hamasen, about 10 minutes across the harbour. Major renovation works are planned along the beach during 2026.

name: Baishawan
description: Baishawan is a beach break in Shimen, New Taipei, facing north. Waves break right over a sand bottom. It works best on N, NNE, NE, ENE, E swell with S or SW (offshore) wind at low to mid tide and suits beginners and up. A crescent-shaped golden-sand beach at the northern tip of Taiwan with mostly right-hand waves. The gentle waves suit beginners and longboarders, but the winter monsoon often leaves it blown out and messy.

name: Beibin
hazards: slippery submerged boulders;rocky entry;strong current after storms
description: Beibin is a rivermouth in Hualien, Hualien County, facing southeast. Waves break left and right over a sand & rock bottom. It works best on ESE, SE, S, SSW swell with WNW or NNW (offshore) wind at low to mid tide and suits beginners to advanced surfers. A rivermouth break at the Meilun Creek mouth in downtown Hualien next to Beibin Park. A long jetty shelters it from northeast monsoon wind; it is good for longboards on small swells and gets hollower on typhoon and winter swells.

name: Chenggong
description: Chenggong is a point break in Chenggong, Taitung County, facing southeast. Waves break left over a reef bottom. It works best on ENE, E, ESE swell with W or WSW (offshore) wind at mid to high tide and suits advanced to expert surfers only. One of the best left-hand point breaks in Taiwan, breaking close to shore over sharp coral reef. Northeast or east typhoon swells produce fast barrels. For experienced to expert surfers only.

name: Daxi
description: Daxi is a beach break in Toucheng, Yilan County, facing southeast. Waves break left and right over a sand with rock bottom. It works best on SE, SSE, S, E swell with NW or W (offshore) wind at mid to high tide and suits beginners to advanced surfers. A half-moon-shaped bay also known as Honeymoon Bay with fairly consistent surf; the southern end offers a powerful right on a good southeast swell. It is about a 10-minute walk from Daxi train station and busy on weekends.

name: Donghe
hazards: strong current near the rivermouth after rain;cobblestone bottom at low tide
description: Donghe is a rivermouth in Donghe, Taitung County, facing east. Waves break left and right over a rock bottom. It works best on E, NE, SE, SSE swell with W or SW (offshore) wind at mid tide and suits intermediate and advanced surfers. A very consistent rivermouth break with a left and a right that gets steady swell in winter. It is cleanest early in the morning and late in the afternoon before the wind picks up.

name: Double Bridge
description: Double Bridge is a rivermouth in Shoufeng, Hualien County, facing east. Waves break left and right over a rock bottom. It works best on E, NE, S, SE swell with W or WNW (offshore) wind at mid tide and suits experienced surfers only. A rivermouth break under the Double Bridge on the Hualien coastal highway. Big swells bring long, clean but heavy and fast waves that can close out onto the rocks; surf with a partner.

name: Double Lions
description: Double Lions is a beach break in Toucheng, Yilan County, facing east. Waves break left and right over a sand bottom. It works best on ENE, E, SE, SSE swell with W or SW (offshore) wind at mid to high tide and suits beginners and up. A fairly consistent beach break with lefts and rights all year: a left along the northern rocks on winter northeast swell and a right along the southern rocks on summer south swell, with a view of Turtle Island.

name: Dulan
description: Dulan is a beach break in Donghe, Taitung County, facing southeast. Waves break left and right over a sand and cobblestone bottom. It works best on ENE, E, SE, SSE swell with W or WNW (offshore) wind at mid to high tide and suits beginners and up. A mile-long open beach break with several peaks and smaller, softer waves than most Taitung spots, which makes it good for beginners. Dulan is a laid-back surf town with surf hostels, an artist community and live music.

name: Duli
hazards: boulders;rip currents;heavy shorebreak on big days;submerged stones
description: Duli is a beach break in Chenggong, Taitung County, facing east. Waves break left and right over a sand with a few submerged rocks bottom. It works best on E, NE, ESE swell with W or WSW (offshore) wind at mid tide and suits beginners and up. A sandy beach break between Chenggong and Donghe whose peaks shift with the sandbars. The most consistent surf arrives from late autumn to spring on east to northeast swell; summer waves are smaller and beginner-friendly.

name: Baxian Dong
description: Baxian Dong is a rivermouth & point break in Changbin, Taitung County, facing east. Waves break left over a sand & rock bottom. It works best on E, NE swell with W or SW (offshore) wind at mid to high tide and suits experienced surfers only. A left-hand point break formed by a rivermouth that is often offshore when the northeast monsoon blows out other spots. Big winter or typhoon swells can produce one of the best barreling lefts in Taiwan; experienced surfers only.

name: Environmental Park
description: Environmental Park is a reef in Hualien, Hualien County, facing east-northeast. Waves break left and right over a cobblestone bottom. It works best on E, SE swell with WNW or NW (offshore) wind at mid tide and suits intermediate and advanced surfers. A remote, hard-to-find spot near a landfill, reached by a bike path and a small cliff. Punchy walls break over a shallow rocky bottom; it is usually blown out in winter and better from spring to autumn.

name: Fulong
hazards: rip currents;strong currents on big days
description: Fulong is a rivermouth beach break in Gongliao, New Taipei, facing northeast. Waves break left and right over a sand bottom. It works best on N, NE, E swell with S or SW (offshore) wind at all tides tide and suits beginners to advanced surfers. A fairly exposed beach break with a sandbar built by the outflow of the Shuang River. The best spot is next to the temple, with a short left into the channel and a long walling right on big days.

name: Gengfang
description: Gengfang is a point break in Toucheng, Yilan County, facing southeast. Waves break left over a sand with rock bottom. It works best on E, NE swell with NW or W (offshore) wind at mid to high tide and suits experienced surfers only. A left-hand point break in a small fishing village north of Wushi Harbor. The pier shields north and northeast wind, and northeast typhoon swells can make the left epic. Advanced surfers only; surf mid to high tide.

name: Gongs
hazards: concrete blocks;large boulder in the take-off zone;closeouts onto rocks
description: Gongs is a reef in Shoufeng, Hualien County, facing east / southeast. Waves break left and right over a sand and cobblestone bottom. It works best on ENE, E, SE swell with W or WSW (offshore) wind at low to mid tide and suits intermediate and advanced surfers. A remote reef break about 200 meters south of a fishing-harbor parking lot. Enter and exit from the harbor pier rather than the beach; there are no surf shops or public facilities.

name: Green Bay
description: Green Bay is a beach break in Wanli, New Taipei, facing northeast. Waves break left and right over a sand bottom. It works best on E, NE swell with W or SW (offshore) wind at mid tide and suits beginners and up. A 1.5 km white-sand beach break between Jinshan and Keelung with many peaks and an easy paddle out. It suits beginners and advanced surfers but is often crowded in summer; there are no surf shops or public bathrooms.

name: Jinshan
description: Jinshan is a beach break & point break in Jinshan, New Taipei, facing northeast. Waves break left and right over a sand with rock bottom. It works best on N, NNE, NE, E, ESE swell with S or SW (offshore) wind at mid tide and suits beginners to advanced surfers. A beach with a left point break at the northern end and a less consistent right that often closes out. Waves are best early morning or evening before the wind; it is often crowded in summer.

name: Jiqi
description: Jiqi is a beach break in Fengbin, Hualien County, facing east. Waves break left and right over a cobblestone bottom. It works best on E, NE, SE swell with W (offshore) wind at mid to high tide and suits beginners to advanced surfers. A long, unsheltered cobblestone beach with two surf areas and many peaks; strong wind often affects wave quality. Surf shops and board rentals are limited.

name: Jiupeng
description: Jiupeng is a beach break & point break in Manzhou, Pingtung County, facing northeast. Waves break left and right over a sand with rock bottom. It works best on E, ESE, SE swell with NW or W (offshore) wind at mid tide and suits intermediate and advanced surfers. A reef headland next to coastal sand dunes in Manzhou. Winter northeast monsoon swell brings shortboard waves, and on southeast swell the headland works as a point break with long peeling rights.

name: Nanwan
description: Nanwan is a beach break in Hengchun, Pingtung County, facing south. Waves break right over a sand with submerged reef bottom. It works best on S, SE, SSW swell with N or NE (offshore) wind at low to mid tide and suits beginners to advanced surfers. Southern Taiwan's most popular beach with a left and a right break. It is good for beginners when small and can barrel on summer typhoon swell, but it is flat for much of the year.

name: Shanshui
description: Shanshui is a beach break in Magong, Penghu, facing south. Waves break left and right over a sand bottom. It works best on S, SE, SW swell with N or NW (offshore) wind at all tides tide and suits beginners and up. An unspoiled beach with clear water on Penghu island, better known for windsurfing in the windy winter; surfing is better in summer.

name: Sheliao
description: Sheliao is a rivermouth & point break in Checheng, Pingtung County, facing west. Waves break left over a sand with rock bottom. It works best on W, SW swell with E (offshore) wind at mid to low tide and suits intermediate and advanced surfers. A rivermouth and left point break at the Baoli River mouth near Guishan Bridge in Checheng. A solid southwest swell with east wind produces some of the longest lefts in Taiwan, but the spot is often flat.

name: Sicao Bridge
description: Sicao Bridge is a beach break in Tainan, Tainan, facing southwest. Waves break left and right over a sand bottom. It works best on S, SW swell with N or NE (offshore) wind at all tides tide and suits beginners and up. A sandy west-coast beach break with shifting lefts and rights, best in summer on typhoon and southwest swells. It is popular with skimboarders and busy with tourists on weekends.

name: Songbai Harbor
description: Songbai Harbor is a beach break in Dajia, Taichung, facing northwest. Waves break left and right over a sand and cobblestone bottom. It works best on N, NW swell with E or SE (offshore) wind at mid to high tide and suits beginners and up. A west-coast beach break flanked by pine and cypress forest, with a tidal range that often exceeds 3 meters. It usually has small waves for beginners and comes alive on certain typhoon swells.

name: Waipu
description: Waipu is a beach break in Houlong, Miaoli County, facing northwest. Waves break left and right over a sand bottom. It works best on N, NW swell with SE or SSE (offshore) wind at mid tide and suits beginners and up. A large west-coast beach break that is a good alternative when the northeast monsoon blows out the northern spots. It is best at mid tide on the incoming tide; there is no parking lot or washing facility.

name: Wanli
description: Wanli is a beach break in Wanli, New Taipei, facing northeast. Waves break left and right over a sand with a few submerged rocks bottom. It works best on NE, E swell with W or SW (offshore) wind at mid to high tide and suits beginners to advanced surfers. A beach break next to Green Bay that a jetty shelters from east and southeast wind, so it can be good when Green Bay is blown out. It is best about two hours before high tide; there are no surf shops.

name: Wuwei Harbor
description: Wuwei Harbor is a beach break in Su'ao, Yilan County, facing northeast. Waves break left and right over a sand & rock bottom. It works best on E, NE swell with SW or WSW (offshore) wind at mid to high tide and suits beginners to advanced surfers. A long beach break near Su'ao with many peaks that is usually inconsistent and gutless, better for longboards and SUPs, but can be epic on a big southeast typhoon swell.

name: Yiwan
hazards: strong rip near the rivermouth;rock bottom
description: Yiwan is a rivermouth & point break in Chenggong, Taitung County, facing southeast. Waves break left over a rock bottom. It works best on NE, ENE, E swell with W or WSW (offshore) wind at mid tide and suits intermediate and advanced surfers. A left point break in Taitung that blocks northeast wind well, with long walls and rides of up to a hundred meters. Not for beginners.

name: Yuguangdao
description: Yuguangdao is a beach break in Anping, Tainan, facing southwest. Waves break left and right over a sand bottom. It works best on S, SW swell with E or NE (offshore) wind at all tides tide and suits beginners and up. A beach break on Yuguang Island in Anping, Tainan, with beginner-friendly peaks. It is best on summer typhoon and southwest swells, inconsistent in January and February, and busy on weekends.

name: Zhu'an
description: Zhu'an is a beach break in Toucheng, Yilan County, facing east. Waves break left and right over a sand bottom. It works best on NE, ENE, E, ESE, SE, SSE swell with WNW or W or WSW (offshore) wind at mid to high tide and suits beginners and up. A long, open beach break exposed to many swell directions but also to wind, so it is often onshore. It is best on typhoon or winter northeast monsoon swell and is usually uncrowded.

name: Zhunan
description: Zhunan is a beach break in Zhunan, Miaoli County, facing northwest. Waves break left and right over a sand bottom. It works best on N, NW, W swell with E or SE (offshore) wind at mid tide and suits beginners and up. A sandy west-coast beach break with calm waves that suit beginners, best early in the morning before the wind; it is also a windsurfing and kitesurfing spot.

name: NSYSU Beach
alt_names: NSYSU;Sizihwan;Sizihwan Bay;Xiziwan;Xizi Wan;Sizi Bay;West Bay;Sun Yat-sen University Beach
description: NSYSU Beach is the campus beach of National Sun Yat-sen University on Sizihwan Bay in Gushan District, Kaohsiung, facing west across the Taiwan Strait. It has a sandy beach with coral reefs and is listed as a beach break with A-frame waves that suits beginners. The university describes Sizihwan as a great spot for beginner surfers in summer, and a student-run project offers free surf lessons with sponsored equipment in exchange for collecting beach litter. NSYSU is the university closest to the ocean in Taiwan, and the Cijin ferry and the Hamasen district are a short distance away.
